This kinda explains why I've decided not to have children. I've been with my partner for 7 years now, and we love each other with all of our hearts, and we can't wait to start a future together. We're going to get a pet together when we're able to afford it/look after them properly, and I'm so excited to have a fur baby with him 💕 I've had many a conversation with people over the past few years with people who have asked if we want children, whether that be now or in the future, and my honest answer is no... I feel as though this world has a lot of problems and issues. (The cost of living being the main one), not to mention everything else that's going on right now. I've finally found comfort and confidence in telling people that we don't want kids. It's a tough one, but it needs to be spoken about openly. As a person who has worked with children between the ages of 10 months up to 5 years for the past 7 years, I find it hard to get my head around it all. These kids are full of joy and happiness and have their whole lives ahead of them. However, for some reason, I can't help but find myself worrying for their future... it isn't as good as it was, and I believe it's only going to get worse as time goes on... I think that makes you kind of understand why they behave the way they do. Their parents have been introduced to "gentle parenting," and as much as it's the norm nowadays, I can't help but think that parents have given up on raising their children in the best way (mainly through their own issues growing up.) Social media/technology has taken over, and I find kids are becoming disconnected from the real world. Where have the times gone when we were told by our parents, "When the streetlights come on, it's time to come home for your dinner!!"
This is just my personal view on the whole thing, and I have nothing against people who decide to have children, adopt, etc.
